messages.text:
Do I have to have received a miner from you before I can download firmware?
I have a SupraHex (6x BM1368) I'd like to check for compatability.

No purchase needed. Harlo OS downloads, release notes and guides are open to anyone at https://harlolabs.com/ , so you can pull the firmware and check it against your SupraHex.

I won't guess on a 6x BM1368 board, since supported models are listed on the site rather than by chip. Fastest read on compatibility is our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , post in the server and mention @nullhashrate (JD). He knows which boards it flashes cleanly.
Before you go, one thing: what's making you look at Harlo OS for the SupraHex, something it's doing now that you want to fix?
Just want to play with the OS before my actual miners arrive from you next month.

That makes sense, good way to get the dashboard and pool setup under your belt before the units land.

One follow-up: what do you most want to have figured out by the time they arrive, the pool side or the tuning?
Tuning. I'll never overclock anything, but just to have the familiarity is a good thing.

Sensible, and worth saying out loud: overclocking voids the warranty, so staying stock is the right call.

Last one: is the tuning about keeping heat and noise down in the observatory, or about squeezing efficiency per watt?
The noise is critical. The observatory is next to the horse corrals and I'd prefer not to spook the horses.

Horses next door is a good reason. Fan speed in Harlo OS is where you'll win that, pulling the fans down a notch and letting the unit sit a bit warmer is usually quieter than anything else you can change.

That's noted on your file for when the units land. Thanks for humouring the questions.
It's all good. Thank you for the questions and help.

Any time. Grab Harlo OS from https://harlolabs.com/ and if the SupraHex gives you trouble, JD and the crowd on Discord will sort you out: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf

A copy of this chat comes to your email once we close it out. Good luck with the build, and say hi to the horses.
